title: The model that grows sideways
summary: A teaching episode on continual learning without another full pretraining run: why sequential updates forget, how replay, regularization, and modular isolation respond, how LoRA specialists and a versioned harness split the learning problem, and which parts of Macaron-V1's continual-learning claim are demonstrated versus still open.

sources.title: Macaron-V1: Towards Open Continual Learning with Self-Improvement and Mixture-of-LoRA
LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks
Beyond Static Models: An Evolving Framework for Continual Learning in Large Language Models across Training Stages

topics: deep dive: continual learning without a fresh pretrain — catastrophic forgetting, replay, regularization, modular isolation, low-rank adapters, specialist routing, model-harness co-design, retention, transfer, and evidence boundaries
concepts_taught: modular continual learning without a fresh pretrain: separate a stable frozen base from low-rank specialist updates and a faster-changing harness; understand rehearsal, importance-weight regularization, and architectural isolation as different stability-plasticity trades; route requests explicitly; and require sequential evidence of new-task learning, old-task retention, forward and backward transfer, end-to-end routing behavior, lineage, and rollback before calling the system a continual learner
